chunks: Hishām ibn Sālim narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled regarding one who mutilated or severely mistreated his slave that he is free. There is no authority for him over him; he is a sāʾibah, free to go and attach himself to whomever he wishes, and if someone guarantees his liability, then he inherits him.

key_terms.سَائِبَةٌ: a freed person left independent without former ownership control
key_terms.لَا سَبِيلَ لَهُ عَلَيْهِ: he has no authority or claim over him
key_terms.نَكَّلَ: to inflict severe punishment or mistreatment

ai.seo_question: What did Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام rule about a slave whose master abused him?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning a slave who was severely abused by his master. The ruling establishes the slave’s freedom, removes the master's authority over him, and explains that if another person assumes legal responsibility for him, inheritance may follow through that bond.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3519 - Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as):

"Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, ruled regarding a person who mistreated his slave that the slave becomes free. There is no authority over him, and he is considered a 'sa'ibah' (free without obligation). He may choose to align himself with whomever he wishes, and if that person guarantees his liability, then he inherits from him."
